boundary_condition: Do not apply this default to rooms that are specifically meant to have separate beds for occupants; for those rooms, keep the requested separate-bed setup such as two twins.
condition: When selecting a bed type for a hotel room where a single main bed is appropriate, use a queen-size bed as the minimum acceptable main bed.
default_action: Request a queen-size or better bed, with a king-size bed acceptable as an upgrade when offered.
exception_condition: If a room has an explicit layout requirement, such as a queen-size bed plus a pull-out couch, preserve that stated layout instead of automatically changing the bed configuration.
name: Queen-or-better hotel bed default
rationale: Across four distinct scripted sources, the user asks for a queen-size bed, queen-size or better, or queen/king. The multi-room example also shows that the queen preference is scoped by room role, since another room separately needs two twins.

source_evidence.contribution: hotel-9 explicitly supports the minimum: "We'd like a queen size or better bed."
hotel-11 repeats the same bed-size threshold: "I'd like a queen-size or better bed."

hotel-8 supports queen as the main-bed choice for one room while showing a separate-bed boundary for another room: "One room needs a queen size and a pull out couch. And, the other room needs two twins."
hotel-10 supports queen as the minimum and king as acceptable: "I'd like a room with either a queen-size or king-size bed."
